I am 63 years old and have farmed these lands in Quzhou for 45 years. With high school education, I read the county extension bulletins, but I trust my eyes more. My wife and I are only two people, so I rely on machinery and efficient practices. My 35 mu are divided into 28 mu of wheat–maize double cropping and 7 mu of cotton. The wheat went in last October with my own saved seed of an improved variety at 40 jin per mu. Now it is greening up, and I will broadcast 60 jin per mu of ammonium chloride as topdressing on top of the 150 jin per mu of 15-15-15 compound I applied as basal. I will irrigate four times from the well—green-up, jointing, heading, and grain-filling—and spray twice for insects, once for weeds, and twice for fungi. After wheat harvest on June 6, I immediately sow summer maize using no-tillage to save the critical ten-day window. I buy Longyu 662 hybrid seed and apply 100 jin per mu of 28-6-6 compound by machine, irrigating twice and spraying twice for insects and once for weeds. For cotton, I plant 7 mu around April 9 with bought improved seed, using rotary tillage and plastic mulch. I broadcast 100 jin per mu of 18-10-20 compound, irrigate twice, and spray heavily—twelve times for insects, twice for weeds, and twice with growth regulator—because bollworm never gives up. My well gives reliable water, but pumping costs electricity, so I do not waste it. After 45 years, I know my land.
